items.title: Kerten CEO Says First India Property by Year-End, Pipeline Likely to Exceed 1,000-Key Target: Exclusive
items.summary: India's hotel market doesn't need another global chain pretending to be local. Kerten Hospitality's entire bet is that developers have finally figured that out too.

items.title: Travelport Launches TripServices to Power AI Travel Booking
items.summary: AI agents can already help travelers dream up trips. Booking them is harder. Travelport is betting that cleaner access to flights, hotels, and extras will keep travel sellers from looking elsewhere.

items.title: Aven’s New Booking Engine Targets Hotel Direct Booking Conversions
items.summary: Aven, the former Sabre hospitality business, is taking direct aim at a core hotel tech problem: how much legacy infrastructure can still support modern direct booking. Its new booking engine shows what a cleaner rebuild could look like.

items.title: Canadian Tourists Bailed On the U.S. — Canadian Airlines Still See Growth
items.summary: As one of the largest travel markets continues to shrink due to political tensions, Canadian carriers told Skift that U.S. travel is still producing healthy margins.

items.title: Hotels Are Hoping For a Last-Minute World Cup Surge. Will It Come?
items.summary: Operators are banking on spur-of-the-moment travel from soccer fans who want to see their favorite teams play in the World Cup. Data suggests there are reasons to be optimistic, but it’s still not clear how big of a surge last-minute bookings will bring.

items.title: Canadian Travel to the U.S. Rebounds, But Still Far Below 2024 Levels
items.summary: Two months of gains is progress — but Canadian trips to the U.S. are still down nearly 29% from two years ago.

items.title: The Most Disciplined New Amenity in Hospitality Isn’t a Spa. It’s a Sandbag
items.summary: Hyatt’s reading of the fitness zeitgeist with its alignment with Hyrox is spot-on. It’s only a matter of time until competitors take notice of the surging sport.

items.title: 4 Bets Accor Is Making on AI and the Future of Hospitality
items.summary: Accor's AI strategy spans discovery, distribution, loyalty, and operations, but its boldest bet is the one focused on people. The company believes automating the invisible half of hotel work is what will let the visible half feel more human.
